scientific_question: Which deployment-visible feature block accounts for the frozen v154 cross-trajectory support failures, and do the failures justify a temporal-phase or geometry correction next?
scope: Post-open root-cause diagnostic on the already sealed v154 train-split nearest-neighbour result. No target, CFD truth, coefficient label, predictor fit, physical replay, validation/test access, resource claim, or real-BOST claim is allowed.

calculation.distance_identity: For each sealed query-neighbour pair, apply the held-out fold's frozen mean and scale to both rows, square their 45 coordinate differences, and require sqrt(sum(delta2)/45) to reproduce the sealed v154 distance.
calculation.block_share: Sum squared standardized differences within each frozen feature block and divide by the all-45 sum.
calculation.rows_reported: All rows and unsupported rows are reported separately for each failed trajectory, camera count and frame.
context_checks: exact frame match rate and absolute frame-index difference

decision_rule.geometry_dominated: If reported_geometry contributes more than half of aggregate unsupported-row squared distance in any failed trajectory, keep a geometry-normalization mechanism eligible for a separately frozen test.
decision_rule.state_dominated: If observation plus K1 residual plus K1 dual contribute at least 75 percent and reported_geometry at most 25 percent for every failed trajectory, classify the gap as deployment-state dominated and do not spend the next run on another geometry-only warp.
decision_rule.mixed: Otherwise classify the evidence as mixed and do not authorize a new mechanism from this diagnostic alone.
decision_rule.temporal_phase: Frame-match statistics are descriptive only. They cannot by themselves authorize a temporal model because the five frozen frame indices are sparse and repeated across perturbation strata.
